facts.fact: Nielsen's research, as cited by StackAdapt, found that brand recall accounts for 38.7% of brand lift in emerging media.
facts.quote: brand recall is the biggest driver of lift in emerging media, accounting for 38.7% of brand lift

facts.fact: As cited by StackAdapt, a Google study found that users who watch ads for more than three seconds experience higher brand awareness, ad recall, and consideration.
facts.quote: users who watch ads for more than three seconds experience higher brand awareness, ad recall, and consideration

facts.fact: StackAdapt's blog states that always-on marketing means marketing activities run continuously every day, year-round, rather than being tied to seasons, events, or specific campaigns.
facts.quote: Always-on marketing is when your marketing efforts are up and running every day, year-round.

facts.fact: StackAdapt describes campaign-based marketing as having a start and end date, unlike always-on marketing which runs continuously.
facts.quote: Campaign-based marketing has a start and end date.

facts.fact: In advertising, always-on means a campaign or tactic that runs continuously and is refreshed over time, rather than being limited to a fixed flight date.
facts.quote: In advertising, always-on means a campaign or tactic that runs continuously and is refreshed over time, rather than being limited to a fixed flight date.

facts.fact: Always-on marketing content is evergreen content that stays relevant over time, such as guides, explainers, FAQs, blog posts, and retargeting creative.
facts.quote: Always-on marketing content is evergreen content that stays relevant over time, such as guides, explainers, FAQs, blog posts, and retargeting creative

facts.fact: Always-on marketing works best when a brand wants to stay visible between major campaigns, support the full funnel, and nurture demand over time.
facts.quote: Always-on marketing works best when a brand wants to stay visible between major campaigns, support the full funnel, nurture demand over time
